title: How do birds know where to migrate?

lines.text: How can a tiny songbird fly five thousand miles across oceans and land in the exact same backyard tree every year?
Birds possess navigational abilities that surpass modern human military guidance systems.
They use the position of the sun during the day, and memorized star constellations at night.
lines.caps: They navigate by the *sun | and nighttime star *constellations

lines.text: They even smell atmospheric odor gradients to track geographic river coastlines.
lines.caps: They smell *chemical scents | carried on ocean *winds

lines.text: Most mind-blowing of all, birds possess quantum compasses in their eyes.
lines.caps: They have *quantum compasses | built into their *eyes!

lines.text: Special proteins called cryptochromes allow birds to literally see Earth's invisible magnetic field lines as shades of light.
lines.caps: Cryptochromes let birds *see | magnetic field lines in the *sky!

lines.text: Birds navigate the globe using quantum physics built directly into their retinas.
lines.caps: Using quantum *physics | to cross the entire *globe!
